title: How to Increase Direct Bookings for a Resort
excerpt: Practical ways for Indian resorts to win more direct bookings: brand-search defence, value-adds instead of price cuts, packages, Google free booking links and winning back OTA guests.
description: Increase direct bookings for your resort: defend brand searches, add value instead of cutting rates, sell packages and win back guests from OTAs.
html:
To increase direct bookings at a resort, make booking with you clearly better without undercutting your OTA rate: protect searches for your own name, show your direct rate on Google, add value such as meals, late checkout or transfers, build packages OTAs do not sell, and give OTA guests a reason to book direct next time.

Understand the OTA billboard effect

Many guests discover a resort on MakeMyTrip, Booking.com or Agoda, then search its name on Google before deciding. Hospitality marketers call this the billboard effect: the OTA listing acts like an advertisement that sends some people to look you up directly. Whether they then book with you or go back to the OTA depends on what they find.

That gives you a practical test. Search your resort's name on a phone, as a guest would. Note what appears above your own website, whether your Google listing shows your direct rate, and whether your site answers the questions the OTA page answered. Each gap is a booking you may be losing at the last step.

OTAs are not the enemy here. They help guests find you. The aim is to make sure that when a guest goes looking for you directly, booking direct is the easy and attractive choice.

Defend searches for your own brand name

When someone types your resort's name, they have already chosen you. If an OTA ad or listing appears above your website, some of them will book there and you pay commission on a guest you had already won.

  • Run a small Google Ads campaign on your brand name. Brand-name clicks are usually inexpensive and put your own site at the top. Send them to your home page or booking page, not a generic page. See PPC management for how we structure this.
  • Keep your Google Business Profile complete. Correct website link, phone, WhatsApp, photos and room details.
  • Make sure your site ranks for your name. A clear title tag with your resort name and location, and a fast mobile page, help here.
  • Check monthly. Search your name, plus "resort", plus your town, and see what has changed.

Add value instead of cutting the price

The instinct is to offer a lower direct rate. That can create problems with OTA agreements and trains guests to shop around. A more durable approach is to keep the room rate in line and make the direct booking include more.

On rate parity specifically: in October 2022, the Competition Commission of India fined MakeMyTrip-Goibibo and directed it to drop "wide" price and room parity obligations relative to other OTAs. It treated "narrow" parity, covering the hotel's own website, as potentially justifiable. Contracts differ, so read your own OTA agreements before changing anything. Value-adds are the usual way to make booking direct better without undercutting the OTA rate.

Value-adds that guests in India respond to:

  • Breakfast or a meal plan included for direct bookings.
  • Guaranteed late checkout or early check-in, subject to availability.
  • Free pick-up from the nearest railway station or bus stand.
  • A guided plantation walk in Coorg, a backwater sunset ride in Kerala, or a bonfire evening.
  • Room upgrade on arrival when available.
  • Flexible cancellation on direct bookings.

State the benefit clearly on your website, on the booking engine page and in your Google listing description. "Book direct: breakfast and late checkout included" is easy to understand. A vague "best rate guaranteed" badge is not.

Build packages that only you can sell

OTAs sell rooms well. They are less suited to selling experiences that need conversation or customisation. Packages are where direct booking has a natural advantage.

  • A two-night anniversary package with a candle-lit dinner and room decoration.
  • A family weekend with kids' activities and a fixed meal plan.
  • A corporate offsite package for 20 to 40 people with meeting space and team activities.
  • A monsoon long-stay offer with a work-friendly room and reliable Wi-Fi.

Each package needs its own clear page with the price, what is included and how to book or enquire. The post on resort landing pages for packages covers how to build them.

Use Google free booking links and metasearch

In Google's hotel results and your business panel, Google can show rates from several sources, including your own site through free booking links. When a guest is comparing, seeing your direct rate beside OTA rates, with the same or better inclusions, makes the direct option visible at the moment of decision.

These connections usually run through your booking engine or channel manager. Ask your provider whether they connect to Google's hotel listings, and check that your rates and availability show correctly once live. Paid Hotel Ads are an option to test later, once you are tracking cost per booking.

Win back guests who found you on an OTA

Every OTA guest who stays with you is a chance to make their next booking direct. Do this honestly and within your OTA agreement; do not ask guests to cancel and rebook.

  1. At check-in, collect a phone number and, with consent, ask if they would like occasional offers on WhatsApp or email.
  2. During the stay, make the WhatsApp number visible in the room for requests, so it becomes the number they remember.
  3. At checkout, hand over a small card with your website and a returning-guest benefit, such as a free meal or upgrade on their next direct stay.
  4. After the stay, send a thank-you message and a review request. A few months later, send a relevant offer for a long weekend or their anniversary month.

Keep the list small and the messages useful. A past guest who receives two relevant messages a year is more likely to return than one who receives a promotion every week.

A direct booking checklist

ItemCheck
Brand searchYour site or ad appears first when your name is searched on a phone
Google listingDirect rate visible; website, phone and WhatsApp correct
Direct benefitOne clear value-add stated on the home page and booking page
PackagesAt least two packages with their own pages
Booking engineTotal price with taxes shown early; UPI accepted
Returning guestsConsent-based WhatsApp or email list, with a returning-guest benefit
TrackingDirect bookings and their cost recorded monthly

For the measurement side, see what hotel marketing data to track.

Frequently asked questions

Can I offer a lower rate on my website than on OTAs?

It depends on your contract. The Competition Commission of India's October 2022 order against MakeMyTrip-Goibibo dealt with wide parity across OTAs and treated narrow parity covering a hotel's own website as potentially justifiable. Read your own agreements before changing rates. Many owners keep rates aligned and add value to direct bookings instead, which avoids the question entirely.

Why do guests who search my name still book on an OTA?

Usually because the OTA appears first, shows reviews and a clear price, and feels safe. If your own result is lower on the page, slower to load, or hides the total price, guests go back to what is familiar. Brand-name ads, a complete Google listing, a clear direct-booking benefit and an easy mobile booking engine address most of this.

Is it worth running ads on my own resort name?

For most resorts with OTA listings, yes. Brand-name clicks tend to be inexpensive because few advertisers compete for them, and each direct booking they protect saves a commission. Start with a small daily budget, track bookings from the campaign, and compare the cost per booking with your OTA commission. Stop if the numbers do not justify it.

How do I get OTA guests to book direct next time?

Give them a reason and a way. Ask for consent to stay in touch at check-in, make your WhatsApp number the one they use during the stay, and give a returning-guest benefit at checkout. Follow up with a thank-you and, later, a relevant offer. Never pressure them to cancel an existing OTA booking.

Where to start

Search your resort's name on your phone today and screenshot what appears above your website. Choose one value-add you can offer every direct guest and add it to your home page and booking engine. Then ask your booking engine provider whether your direct rate can appear in Google's hotel results.
